title: A reduced stack with quasi-compact inertia has a dense open gerbe
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Use algebraic stacks [def-sfb-algebraic-moduli-stack], algebraic spaces [def-trf-algebraic-space], and morphisms and $2$-fibre products of fibred groupoids [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids]. Quasi-compactness is [def-sfb-stack-qcqs-morphism], and point spaces have the topology of [lem-sfb-stack-point-topology]. Let $\mathcal X/S$ be an algebraic stack which is reduced, meaning that it admits a smooth surjective scheme atlas whose local rings have no nonzero nilpotents. Define $I_{\mathcal X/S}=\mathcal X\times_{\mathcal X\times_S\mathcal X}\mathcal X$, with both maps the relative diagonal; its projection to $\mathcal X$ is the inertia projection (equivalently, it forgets the automorphism in a pair $(x,\alpha:x\xrightarrow{\sim}x)$). Suppose this projection is quasi-compact. Then there exist an algebraic open substack $\mathcal U\subseteq\mathcal X$, an algebraic space $Q/S$, and a gerbe $p:\mathcal U\to Q$, such that $|\mathcal U|$ is open and dense in $|\mathcal X|$. An open substack is a strictly full substack whose pullback by every scheme is an open subscheme. A morphism $p:\mathcal U\to Q$ to an algebraic space is a gerbe if for every scheme $T\to Q$ its fibre groupoid has objects fppf locally on $T$, and any two objects of that fibre groupoid are isomorphic fppf locally on $T$ [def-pc-fppf-site]. No quasi-compactness of $\mathcal X$, Noetherianity, finite-type hypothesis, or quasi-separatedness hypothesis is imposed. The empty stack is allowed.

source.place: Tag 06RC (proposition-open-stratum); gerbe means a gerbe over an algebraic space, as in the discussion preceding proposition-when-gerbe.

proof.text: Choose the reduced smooth surjective atlas $p:P\to\mathcal X$ supplied by the hypothesis, and write $x\in\mathcal X(P)$ for its object. Put $R=P\times_{\mathcal X}P$, with source and target $s,t$, and $G=\operatorname{Aut}_P(x)$. The representable diagonal and [lem-sfb-stack-diagonal-space-source-representability] make $R$ an algebraic space. Its two projections are smooth surjective base changes of $p$ by [lem-sfb-stack-chartwise-smooth-etale-calculus]. The scheme pullback of inertia along $p$ is $G$: an object consists of $(y,\alpha,a:x\simeq y)$, which is sent to $a^{-1}\alpha a\in\operatorname{Aut}(x)$; the inverse uses $y=x,a=1$. These mutually inverse identifications respect pullback. By [lem-sfb-inertia-locally-finite-type], $G\to P$ is locally of finite type. Quasi-compactness of the inertia projection, through [lem-sfb-representable-stack-quasicompact-tests], says its scheme base change $G\to P$ is quasi-compact as a map of algebraic spaces. Thus this map is of finite type over the reduced scheme $P$.

source.place: Tag 06RC (proposition-open-stratum), choose a presentation; Tag 06PR (lemma-presentation-inertia), objectwise identification written out; Tag 050Q (lemma-inertia).

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-space-maximal-flat-lfp-base-open] to $G\to P$ and call its largest good base open $W$. Its existence requires no finiteness assumptions. Every etale scheme chart of $P$ is reduced by [etale-proposition-etale-reduced], so $P$ is reduced in the sense of the next node. Apply [lem-sfb-space-reduced-generic-flat-finite-presentation] to this finite-type morphism over reduced $P$, obtaining a dense open $D\subseteq P$ where the stabilizer is flat and locally of finite presentation. The maximality clause gives $D\subseteq W$, so $W$ is dense in $P$. In particular no finiteness assertion about the irreducible components of $P$ is used.

source.place: Tag 06RC, largest W and density; spaces-morphisms.tex Tag 06QS; spaces-descent.tex Tag 06R2. Etale charts of the reduced atlas are reduced: etale.tex Tag 025O.

proof.text: The two pullbacks $s^*G$ and $t^*G$ to $R$ are isomorphic: an arrow $r:x_a\xrightarrow{\sim}x_b$ sends an automorphism $g$ of $x_a$ to $rgr^{-1}$ of $x_b$; conjugation by $r^{-1}$ is the inverse. This formula is natural on every test scheme, hence is an isomorphism of the representing spaces over $R$. Since $s,t$ are smooth, they are flat and locally of finite presentation by [lem-sfb-stack-chartwise-smooth-etale-calculus]. The pullback equality of [lem-sfb-space-maximal-flat-lfp-base-open] identifies the maximal good base opens of $s^*G$ and $t^*G$ with $s^{-1}W$ and $t^{-1}W$. The conjugation isomorphism gives equality of these opens. Thus $W$ is invariant under the presentation relation, as an equality of open subspaces rather than only of geometric points.

source.place: Tag 06R4 (lemma-property-G-invariant), conjugation argument with Tag 06R2; the conjugation map and inverse are written explicitly.

proof.text: By [lem-sfb-invariant-open-substack-descent], the invariant open $W\subseteq P$ corresponds to an open substack $\mathcal U\subseteq\mathcal X$ with $P\times_{\mathcal X}\mathcal U=W$. The restricted map $W\to\mathcal U$ is smooth surjective, being the base change of $p$, by [lem-sfb-stack-chartwise-smooth-etale-calculus]. The diagonal of $\mathcal U$ is the restriction of that of $\mathcal X$, and is representable by algebraic spaces: an isomorphism between two objects in a strictly full substack is exactly the same isomorphism as in $\mathcal X$. $\mathcal U$ is an etale stack: its isomorphism sheaves are those of $\mathcal X$, and if an object $x\in\mathcal X(T)$ restricts into $\mathcal U$ on an etale cover $\{T_i\to T\}$, then the open subscheme $T\times_{\mathcal X}\mathcal U\subseteq T$ contains the images of all $T_i$, so it is $T$ and $x\in\mathcal U(T)$. Therefore $W$ is a smooth scheme atlas and $\mathcal U$ is algebraic by [def-sfb-algebraic-moduli-stack].

source.place: Tag 06RC, descent of the invariant open; stacks-properties.tex Tag 0507 (lemma-substacks-presentation), open case.

proof.text: The point-topology theorem [lem-sfb-stack-point-topology] makes $|p|$ continuous and surjective. The inverse image of $|\mathcal U|$ is $|W|$ by the cartesian open square. To check this on field-valued representatives, membership in the open substack is unchanged by an isomorphism after a field extension, and a point of a scheme lies in an open subscheme exactly when its field-valued representative factors through it. Thus $|\mathcal U|$ is open by the atlas criterion. For any nonempty open $O\subseteq|\mathcal X|$, its inverse image in $|P|$ is nonempty open and meets the dense set $|W|$. Its image lies in $O\cap|\mathcal U|$, proving density. If $P$ is empty then $\mathcal X$ is empty and the same assertion is vacuous.

source.place: Tag 06RC, density of the descended open, using the quotient topology of stacks-properties.tex Tag 04XL (lemma-topology-points).

proof.text: Strict fullness identifies $I_{\mathcal U/S}$ with $I_{\mathcal X/S}\times_{\mathcal X}\mathcal U$: its objects are precisely $u\in\mathcal U(T)$ equipped with automorphisms of that same object in $\mathcal X(T)$, and the arrows obey the same conjugation equation. Pulling its projection back along the smooth surjective atlas $W\to\mathcal U$ therefore gives $G_W\to W$. This map is flat and locally of finite presentation by the defining property of $W$. The projection is representable by algebraic spaces by [lem-sfb-inertia-locally-finite-type]. Since the atlas is flat locally finitely presented by [lem-sfb-stack-chartwise-smooth-etale-calculus], [lem-sfb-representable-fppf-etale-open-descent] descends both properties from $G_W\to W$ to $I_{\mathcal U/S}\to\mathcal U$.

source.place: Tag 06RC, final paragraph; inertia restriction is the open-immersion instance of Tag 06R5 (lemma-monomorphism-cartesian-square-inertia), proved here on objects; descent Tags 06PZ and 06Q8.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-flat-inertia-algebraic-space-quotient] to $\mathcal U$: it gives the algebraic space $Q$ which is the fppf sheafification of $T\mapsto\operatorname{Ob}(\mathcal U(T))/\cong$, and its natural map $\pi:\mathcal U\to Q$. This cited statement alone does not assert the gerbe clause, which we now check. The etale-stack convention is an fppf stack by [lem-sfb-etale-smooth-atlas-fppf-descent]. For every scheme $T\to Q$, the local-representative assertion of [lem-weil-pbc-site-sheafification-sections-local] gives an fppf cover on which its section of $Q$ is represented by an object of $\mathcal U$. If two objects of the fibre over this section are given, their isomorphism classes have equal images in $Q(T)$; the local-equality assertion of that same node gives an fppf cover where the classes agree, hence where an isomorphism of the two objects exists by the definition of isomorphism classes. Every such isomorphism lies over the identity section in the discrete sheaf $Q$. These are exactly the two gerbe conditions in the statement, after every $T\to Q$. This also yields the empty gerbe over the empty algebraic space when $\mathcal X$ is empty.

source.place: Tag 06QJ (proposition-when-gerbe), conclusion via Tag 06QD (lemma-gerbe-over-iso-classes); gerbe conditions checked from the local-section and local-equality sheafification theorem, Tags 00WB and 00WK.
